person.name: Anthony V. Lambie
person.text: Associate Vice President on the **technology side of TD marketing**. A York University alumni profile describes him as AVP of Marketing, Collaboration and Internet Technology, leading the IT team that **builds and supports TD's marketing and internet applications and sets their strategic roadmap** (also listed as Head of CX Engagement & Marketing Technology). He joined TD in **2013**. Before that: about 7.5 years at **American Express** supporting marketing and contact-centre technology across seven markets, then **AVP CRM and Contact Centre Solutions at Sun Life Financial**. BA in Political Science, York University. He is a **technology buyer/owner, not the creative or brand lead** — expect questions on integration, security, data and IT approval. Exact current title and team size: to be confirmed on LinkedIn.

company.text: TD Bank Group is one of Canada's largest banks, headquartered in Toronto, serving **over 28.1 million clients** with **13M+ active mobile users** in Canada and the US. In the US, TD Bank runs about **1,048 retail stores** in 15 states and D.C. (as of Jul 31, 2026). In Canada, TD Canada Trust runs roughly **1,000+ branches** (to be confirmed). On **Feb 9, 2026** TD launched **'More Human'**, its first single brand identity across Canada and the US, with a new visual identity by **Jones Knowles Ritchie** and creative by **Publicis Canada**. TD says the rollout runs across platforms and touchpoints through the year and that it wants to keep its branch-centric identity while pushing to 70% digital adoption. Global CMO is **Tyrrell Schmidt** (since Dec 2023). TD also built **TD AI Prism**, an in-house predictive AI model used for marketing personalization.

financials.country: Canada, listed (TSX/NYSE: TD) · fiscal year ends Oct 31
financials.text: **Fiscal 2025 (to Oct 31, 2025):** revenue **C$67.8B** reported / **C$61.8B** adjusted; net income **C$20.5B** reported (boosted by the C$8.6B gain on selling its Schwab stake) / **C$15.0B** adjusted; adjusted EPS C$8.37. CET1 ratio 14.7%. New strategy: **Deeper Relationships, Simpler & Faster, Disciplined Execution**. Restructuring of ~C$825M with **~C$750M targeted annual savings** and ~3% workforce reduction. Still under US AML remediation (about US$500M spend expected in fiscal 2026). **Fiscal 2026 full-year results are due early December 2026** (not yet published).

industry.title: Approval bottlenecks are the pain
industry.text: Bank marketing content goes through brand, legal and compliance sign-off. Industry write-ups (e.g. Merkle, 2026) describe workflows that are slow, fragmented and 'linear and approval-driven'.

industry.title: Banks are buying workflow automation now
industry.text: On **Oct 29, 2026** NatWest added Adclear AI agents to its marketing approval workflow (built into Workfront) and reported **80% faster approvals** with one audit trail. A timely, concrete peer example.

industry.title: Rebrands drive in-branch spend
industry.text: A new identity across ~2,000+ branches/stores means signage, brochures, displays and POS. That is Altavia's core print/POSM territory, where up to **70% of in-store materials are never installed**.

industry.title: Cost pressure on big Canadian banks
industry.text: TD's own savings target and job cuts mean marketing ops must do more with less: a direct case for supplier consolidation and automated quotes.

talking_points: How does TD marketing handle a request today, from brief to quote to approval to delivery? Which tools touch it (Workfront, Adobe, in-house)?
With the 'More Human' rebrand rolling out, how are branch and store materials being briefed, produced and deployed across Canada and the US?
How many print and POSM suppliers does TD use, and who owns supplier selection and quotes — marketing, procurement, or each line of business?
Where do compliance and legal approvals slow things down most?
What does your marketing technology roadmap look like for 2027, and where would a workflow layer like Kazaar fit?
What does IT need to see to approve a new marketing platform (security review, SSO, data residency in Canada)?
Who else should join a follow-up — brand, procurement, or branch marketing?
